# Colombia FIFA World Cup 2026 preview: Diaz, Rodriguez key to Los Cafeteros’ fortunes
[...]
## Colombia will need some magic from the boot of Luis Diaz and James Rodriguez to progress further at FIFA World Cup 2026.
[...]
After missing out on the World Cup four years back, Colombia qualified for the quadrennial event after finishing third in CONMEBOL qualifying. The side lost just four out of the 18 games it played and managed to seal its place with a game to spare.
[...]
Nestor Lorenzo, who was part of the coaching staff in the country’s run to the quarterfinal in 2014, will be looking to bring back that feel good factor from a decade ago. So there is no surprise that he has brought back James Rodriguez into the fold.
[...]
Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz is the main attacking threat and led the charts for the team in qualifying with six goals. He was ably supported by Luis Suarez (four goals) who is quickly developing into a striker to watch out for in Europe after his solid campaign for Sporting Lisbon where he recorded 35 G/A in 32 games.
[...]
Colombia also boasts of an experienced backline who have spent years sharpening their tools in Europe. Yerry Mina has been a mainstay at centre back and will be supported by Davinson Sanchez and defensive midfielder Jefferson Lerma in his quest to protect the clean sheet.
[...]
La Tricolor will be the second favourite to qualify out of Group K containing Portugal, DR Congo and Uzbekistan and will need some magic from the boot of Diaz and Rodriguez to progress further.
[...]
Luis Diaz: Leaving the reigning Premier League champion for the Bundesliga seemed a risky move at the start of the 2025-26 season. But 49 goal contributions and three trophies later, he has cemented himself as one of Europe’s best wingers and will look to put on a show on the left flank at the World Cup.

Beyond the headline duo, Lorenzo has built a balanced, tactically disciplined team that defends well and counter-attacks with venom. They are the clear second seeds in Group K behind Portugal and arguably the group’s most complete all-round side after the favourites.
[...]
Colombia should expect to advance from Group K — most likely as runners-up behind Portugal, with a realistic shot at topping it. With their ranking, talent and form, anything less than reaching the knockout rounds would be underwhelming.
[...]
Beyond the group, Colombia have the quality to threaten a deep run. A quarter-final appearance is a reasonable target, matching their 2014 high-water mark, and on their day they could push further.
[...]
The expanded format and their favourable seeding make Los Cafeteros one of the smart picks for a potential dark-horse run.
[...]
Under Néstor Lorenzo, Colombia are built on tactical discipline, defensive solidity and lethal controlled transitions. They typically set up in a 4-2-3-1 with a double pivot (Lerma plus a partner) protecting the back four, James pulling the strings as the central creator, and
[...]

[...]

[...]
Colombia should comfortably qualify from Group K, most likely as runners-up behind Portugal, with an outside chance of topping the group. Beyond that, a run to the quarter-finals is a realistic and reasonable expectation, with the talent to threaten further. Most likely outcome: knockout-round football and a genuine dark-horse run that reminds the world of their 2014 heroics.
